title: A holiday story
goal: Put everything you've learned into one complete story, meet the *-miş* form, and say goodbye properly.
bekal: telling the story of a trip from start to finish
recognizing *-miş* as the marker for news you didn't witness yourself
saying goodbye and thank you in different situations

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Kapadokya'dan sonra
dialogs.intro: Monday morning in class. Ayşe asks about the weekend trip; the whole class is listening.

lines.speaker: Ayşe:
lines.id: Budi, how was Cappadocia? Come on, tell us.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: It was the two best days of my life.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Gece otobüsüyle. Cuma akşam kalktık, sabah beşte vardık.
lines.id: By night bus. We left Friday evening and arrived at five in the morning.
lines.literal: night bus-its-with. Friday evening departed-we, morning five-at arrived-we.

lines.speaker: Ayşe:
lines.id: Did you go up in a balloon?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Bindik! Çok pahalıydı ama pişman değilim.
lines.id: We did! It was really expensive, but I don't regret it.
lines.literal: boarded-we! very expensive-was but regretful not-I.

lines.speaker: Ayşe:
lines.id: What was it like up there?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Sessizdi. Aşağıda yüzlerce balon vardı, güneş yeni doğuyordu.
lines.id: Silent. There were hundreds of balloons below, and the sun was just rising.
lines.literal: silent-was. below-at hundred-s balloon there-was, sun newly was-rising.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: He went, but he didn't get in the balloon. Apparently he was scared!

lines.speaker: Ayşe:
lines.text: Yine mi? Geçen sene de aynı şeyi yapmış.
lines.id: Again? Apparently he did the same thing last year.
lines.literal: again question? past year also same thing-(object) did-apparently.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Yaz tatilinde tekrar gideceğim. Bu sefer Emre'yi de bindireceğim!
lines.id: I'm going again in the summer holidays. This time I'll get Emre on board too!
lines.literal: summer holiday-its-in again will-go-I. this time Emre-(object) too will-make-board-I!

notes: **Korkmuş means "apparently he was scared", not "he was scared".** The *-miş* form marks news you didn't witness yourself: you heard it from someone else, worked it out from the evidence, or are passing it on as hearsay.

**Hayatımın en güzel iki günüydü** stacks up almost the whole module: the possessive suffix, the noun + noun chain, the *en* form, and the past suffix on a noun. If you can read this sentence without stopping, you've reached the end of A1.

**Doğuyordu is two tenses at once** — ongoing, in the past: "was rising at that moment". The *-yordu* form sets the scene of a story, while *-di* tells what happened. It's A2 material, but you'll hear it in every story.

**Bindireceğim** — "I'll make him get on" — shows the causative *-dir*: *binmek* (to board) → *bindirmek* (to put on board). Turkish makes new verbs out of old ones, and that's one of the gifts waiting for you at A2.

sections.title: The -miş form: news you didn't witness

blocks.text: Turkish has a tool English doesn't: a marker for the **source of information**. If you saw it yourself, use *-di*. If you heard it from someone, read it, or worked it out, use *-miş*.

head: -di form
-miş form
The difference
rows: I saw him come / Apparently he came
I saw the rain / The streets are wet, so it must have rained
I know firsthand / I heard it from someone
I experienced it myself / Apparently it was nice

blocks.text: It follows four-way vowel harmony and consonant harmony: *gelmiş*, *almış*, *olmuş*, *görmüş*, *gitmiş*, *bakmış*. The person endings are the first set: *gelmişim*, *gelmişsin*, *gelmiş*, *gelmişiz*, *gelmişsiniz*, *gelmişler*.

blocks.title: Why fairy tales always use -miş
items: Every Turkish fairy tale begins *Bir varmış, bir yokmuş* — "once there was, once there wasn't". Since the storyteller didn't witness it, the whole tale is told in the *-miş* form.
The form is also used for surprises about yourself: *Uyuyakalmışım!* (I must have overslept!). You didn't witness yourself falling asleep — you only realized it afterward.

blocks.text: At A1 you don't need to produce it yet. What you do need: to **recognize** it, so you know the person you're talking to is passing on news, not an eyewitness account.
An A1 travel story is built from four forms you already have. Notice how this one paragraph uses all four:

blocks.title: Kapadokya — bir hafta sonu
items: *Şimdi o sabahı her gün hatırlıyorum.* (present — now)

blocks.text: *Neyse* is the story-saver: it's used to skip the unimportant bits and carry on — "anyway...". You'll hear it in every long story a Turk tells.
Saying thank you and meaning it

blocks.title: The last sentence of this module
items: *Türkçe öğrenmek kolay değil, ama sen başardın.* — "Learning Turkish isn't easy, but you did it."
Read that sentence once more. Six months ago it was just a string of letters; now you can take apart every piece of it. That's the whole point of these twenty units.

blocks.title: The big review
items: Close the whole module and rebuild these ten sentences from memory: "My name is ..." · "I'm from ..." · "Is there any water?" · "Do you have brothers or sisters?" · "Where are you?" · "I don't understand." · "What time is it?" · "Where are you going?" · "How much is it?" · "Yesterday I went to Sultanahmet."
If eight out of ten come out without stopping to think, you've reached A1 — and you're ready for whatever comes next.

exercises.prompt: Which form is right: *-di* or *-miş*? Write the sentence.
items: Ayşe tells you that Emre has arrived. ____
You got caught in the rain earlier. ____
You wake up and the streets are wet. ____
You ate the mantı and it was good. ____
Your friend says the mantı was good. ____

exercises.prompt: Complete the story with the past tense.
items: Çok pahalı ____. (olmak, past of an adjective)
It was the two best days of my life.
We went up in a balloon.
I'm going there again in the summer holidays.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: Emre geldi. — Emre gelmiş. — Yağmur yağdı. — Yağmur yağmış. — Mantı güzeldi. — Mantı güzelmiş.
bindik — vardık — soğuktu — bindim — pahalıydı — döndük
Anlat bakalım, Kapadokya nasıldı? — Hayatımın en güzel iki günüydü. — Balona bindik. — Pişman değilim. — Yaz tatilinde tekrar gideceğim. — Kendine iyi bak!
Anlat bakalım Kapadokya'yı. — Cuma akşam otobüse bindik. — Çok pahalıydı ama pişman değilim. — Aşağıda yüzlerce balon vardı. — Yaz tatilinde tekrar gideceğim. — Kendine iyi bak.
